gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the OUPES Exodus 1200, the model four of its nine results are about, is listed as sold out on oupes.com today at $549, so a shopper wanting about 1 kWh from OUPES now chooses between the Mega 1 Lite at $599 (1,024 Wh, 2,000 W, 26.8 lb) and the Mega 1 at $699, while BLUETTI sells the 1,024 Wh Elite 100 V2 for $499.
standout_why: I compared against shopsavvy.com (Exodus 1200, updated 2026-02-15, no price), activegearreview.com (Exodus 1200, Jan 2025: $699 list / $349 promo), maketecheasier.com (1100W/1200W, 2022–2024: $809.99) and nerdtechy.com (1100W, 2021, no price). The oupes.com result pages are the store's own listings and compare nothing. None of the review pages says the Exodus 1200 is sold out. None shows the current Exodus 350/700 or Mega 1/1 Lite prices. None prices a rival brand at the same capacity: nerdtechy names only BLUETTI AC200 Max, AC300 and EB70, with no prices.
decides: It changes the pick. The model the results are mostly about can't be bought from OUPES today. The OUPES pick at about 1 kWh becomes the Mega 1 Lite: $599, or $489 with the code on its page, which says only 1 of 100 is left at that price. Choose the Mega 1 at $699 only if you want B2 expansion to 5.12 kWh. Without that need, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (Dealectric lists it) gives the same 1,024 Wh for $499, $100 less than the Mega 1 Lite's full price, at 1,800 W instead of 2,000 W. For smaller needs, the Exodus 700 at $399 for 576 Wh is OUPES's cheapest in-stock pick above 500 Wh.
